newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, Hungary finalise terms of trade deal.
newsitem.headline: Israel, Hungary finalise terms of trade deal.

text.p: Israel and Hungary have finalised the terms of a trade agreement to scrap most duties on imports, Israel's ministry of industry and trade said on Sunday.

The agreement, which will come into force on January 1, 1998, will abolish custom duties on most imports, including industrial products, food and agricultural products, agricultural and irrigation equipment and medical and diagnostic products.
On some products, like textiles, customs will be abolished only in 1999 and in the year 2000.
In 1996, Israel's exports to Hungary totalled $60 million and imports from Hungary totalled $45 million, the ministry said.

Zohar Peri, head of the foreign trade administration at the ministry, said the absence of a free trade agreement was delaying business deals between the two countries and had raised concern the level of trade could fall.
The ministry did not say when the agreement would be signed.
